item.title: Trump and Xi Jinping will hold talks in Washington on trade, AI and more
item.description:
President lays out red carpet as treasury secretary announces extension of ‘Busan agreement’ pausing trade war hostilities AI, trade, Taiwan and climate: what will and won’t be on agenda at Trump-Xi summit Donald Trump has welcomed Xi Jinping to the US, taking the unusual step of greeting the Chinese leader on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews to kick off his state visit to Washington. Xi’s plane was met with a lavish arrival ceremony that included a 30-metre-long (100ft) red carpet flanked by US service members, a military flyover by two B-1 bombers and a presentation of the flags and national anthems of both countries. item.title: UN delegates walk out as Benjamin Netanyahu prepares to address general assembly – video
item.description:
Palestinian president Mahmud Abbas told the UN on Thursday that Israeli policies no longer just jeopardized a two-state solution but were now threatening the "very life and existence" of his people. Abbas delivered prerecorded remarks to the UN’s General Assembly from his office in Ramallah after the United States denied him and other top Palestinian officials visas to attend the gathering for the second year in a row.

item.title: Did El Niño turn Hurricane Polo into the most powerful storm of the season?
item.description:
Polo, with sustained winds of 165mph, is churning 215 miles south of Zihuatanejo but is unlikely to directly hit Mexico A tropical storm off the south-west coast of Mexico has intensified into a category 5 monster in fewer than 24 hours, fueled by stronger than usual El Niño weather patterns in the Pacific Ocean. Hurricane Polo was sending out maximum sustained winds of 165mph (266km/h) on Tuesday as its center churned about 215 miles (346km) south of the coastal city of Zihuatanejo, in Guerrero state. item.description:
UNITED NATIONS — Saudi Arabia's foreign minister warned Thursday that the growing threat from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis extends far beyond his country's borders, calling for international cooperation to protect critical shipping routes after Saudi forces intercepted six ballistic missiles launched toward the kingdom. Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud told Fox News Digital that Riyadh was coordinating with Washington and other international partners as Houthi attacks threatened Saudi territory and commercial shipping in the Red Sea. The Saudi-led coalition said Thursday that its air defenses had intercepted six ballistic missiles allegedly launched by the Houthis toward the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu, according to Reuters. It was not immediately clear whether the attacks caused casualties or damage.…

item.title: Thousands Rally Against Trump’s Kennedy Center Takeover
item.description:
President Trump’s mindset when it comes to the Kennedy Center is that of an authoritarian toddler: If he can’t have the toys he wants, he’ll try to break them and make sure no one else can have them, either. Thousands of furious DC-area residents and Kennedy Center patrons gathered in front of the arts center last week in protest of the president’s threats to tear the building down if he’s not allowed to inscribe his own name on its exterior. item.title: Schism with rebel Catholic sect casts a pall over Pope Leo’s visit to France
item.description:
The Vatican’s recent excommunication of followers of a Catholic splinter sect, the Society of Saint Pius X, has revived a longstanding feud within the Roman Catholic Church ahead of Pope Leo XIV’s state visit to France. The ultra-conservative group has established an extensive network of schools and has attracted thousands of followers in France.

item.title: What's at stake during the meeting between Trump and Xi
item.description:
Today, President Donald J. Trump and Chairman Xi Jinping are set to hold bilateral talks on trade and artificial intelligence. While this may appear to be a promising avenue for cooperation, one of the Trump administration’s top priorities should be to secure the release of political and religious prisoners held hostage by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). This concept is not purely sentiment. It is leverage. When America leads with our values instead of our shopping list, we set the terms. Defending religious freedom on American soil is how you push back against CCP transnational repression and remind Beijing that cooperation is not a blank check. As Americans, we must stand up for religious freedom in all countries, for all people. item.title: ICE has wasted tens of millions of dollars with 'uninformed' detention plans, GAO finds
item.description:
GAO documents array of costly problems as ICE pursues controversial plans to rapidly increase detention capacity US Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) and other federal agencies have wasted tens of millions of dollars pursuing controversial plans to rapidly increase detention capacity – and the total will likely rise due to continuing mismanagement, congressional investigators warned on Thursday. The US government accountability office (GAO) documented costly problems in several initiatives ICE has pursued since Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025 and ordered the mass arrest and deportation of people his administration has deemed should be forced out of the country.
